Use case: illustration-story. Production Korean minhwa 2D game asset: ONE complete straight horizontal Ojakgyo bridge formed entirely by a tightly connected flock of crows and magpies, their layered wings and backs forming a continuous walkable narrow ribbon. Long landscape composition approximately 3:1. The two endpoints are at the same height. Near-top view with very shallow depth drawn entirely in ink; a clear continuous upper center walking band, organic feather edges, no gaps large enough to lose the walking surface. About 12-16 distinct small birds, modest repeated rhythm rather than a chaotic swarm. Restrained Joseon minhwa style: fine sepia outlines, charcoal feather hatching, warm ivory wings, muted gray-green and blue-gray washes, subtle antique paper texture ONLY inside the painted silhouettes. Hand-painted, delicate, organic; no vector shapes, rectangles, planks, geometric platforms, rails, perspective convergence, 3D render, terrain, shadow or surrounding sky. Genuine transparent alpha around the bridge with 12% clear margin. No gradient background, glow, checkerboard, text or watermark. This flat bitmap will supply all visible bridge geometry across a ramp in a Korean paper-collage puzzle game; preserve a simple straight readable span so it can be oriented toward either cardinal direction.

Transparent game sprite atlas, 2 by 2 evenly spaced grid: Korean folktale Gyeonwu and Jiknyeo couple holding hands. Top left front view, top right right-side profile, bottom left back view, bottom right left-side profile. Each cell contains the same two full-length adults in traditional hanbok, man with traditional hat and woman with ribbon. CHARCOAL INK SILHOUETTES, restrained warm gray internal brush strokes, traditional Korean minhwa watercolor illustration. No landscape. No paper background. No glow, no blur, no shadow outside the figures. Truly transparent background between and around the figures. Consistent height and baselines. Generous empty transparent margins in each cell, no grid lines, no text.
